newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Volker chief sees 1996 ordinary net up 12-20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Volker chief sees 1996 ordinary net up 12-20 pct.

text.p: Construction firm Koninklijke Volker Stevin NV said on Wednesday it expected 1996 ordinary net profits to rise by 12 to 20 percent.

"First-half net profits were buoyed by an extraordinary gain but also without (these) we expect a significant increase in full-year profits...of between 12 and 20 percent," chairman Aad Baardewijk told a news conference.
The company earlier reported first-half net profits jumped to 16.1 million guilders from a year-earlier 10.3 million.
But the bottom line was boosted by a 4.1 million guilder book profit from the sale in May of a majority stake in its Ecotech environmental services unit to Dutch power company UNA.
Excluding the gain, first-half profits picked up 1.7 million guilders to 12.0 million, or 2.40 guilders per share compared with a year-earlier 2.10 guilders.
The company earlier said it expected an increase of at least 15 percent in earnings per share over full-year 1996, based on a limited conversion of a subordinated bond.
